objective: Invent and build a completely new, simple Godot game from the neutral baseline. Discover one immediately readable player verb and one consequential decision, prove a short deterministic interaction in the real engine, then take exactly one representative encounter through approved whole-screen scene targets into a coherent production-ready pixel-art slice with authored UI, causal animation, planning/action/result states, and honest evidence. Keep scope ruthlessly small; do not reuse the concept, fiction, composition, or mechanics of earlier GameFactory games.

nodes.instructions: Find the smallest interaction that proves the game hypothesis. Return pass when the mechanic, deterministic scenario, and explicit non-goals are bounded; use needs_advisor only for a material capability gap.

Define a feasible engine-native visual system for one representative encounter. Specify native pixel grid, palette, typography, sprite and animation contracts, UI surfaces, anti-patterns, and what must be proven in an engine capture. ImageGen outputs are reference or source only. Return a structured production plan without prescribing a single composition.

Build only the smallest honest Godot graybox and deterministic scenario. Label every visual surface and asset as prototype. Do not spend time manufacturing polish and do not claim production maturity.

Run the real Godot scenario and inspect causal feedback. Return pass only when the bounded mechanic works and evidence is honest; return revise with concrete defects otherwise. Do not judge visual polish here.

Create whole-screen visual targets before any individual production asset is generated. Use the proven graybox at the shipping camera and the visual-director handoff to generate multiple coherent full-scene candidates, then propose one selected direction plus the required whole-scene state variants (for example planning, selection, action, and result when applicable). Review your proposal for gameplay clarity, hierarchy, legibility, plausible controls, state comprehension, engine feasibility, character-to-UI balance, and absence of contradictory or decorative nonsense. Write a valid gamefactory.scene-target/v1 manifest to design/scene-targets/scene-target.json: hash every candidate view, preserve exact prompts, select one candidate and primary view, define nativeGeometry, and map components with sourceViewId, crop, stateIds, and derivedFromSceneTargetSha256. Leave component.production absent because no isolated asset exists yet. Set approval.status to needs-revision, reviewer to pending-scene-target-gate, and selectedTargetSha256 to the selected primary view hash. Do not generate individual UI or gameplay assets yet. Return revise yourself if no complete scene is strong enough to propose.

Review every proposed full-scene target at the shipping camera before component production begins. Verify that the screen communicates the actual gameplay, interaction hierarchy, selected/action/result states, readable text zones, relative scale, navigation, and engine-feasible composition. Reject impressive concept art, nonsensical controls, ambiguous state, decorative clutter, inconsistent internal scale, or a target that cannot be decomposed into reusable components. Return pass only with one explicitly approved target id and hash plus approved state variants and component map; otherwise return revise with prioritized scene-level changes. This gate judges the complete screen, not isolated assets.

Record the passed scene-target-gate decision without changing its creative work. Read the gate's selected target id, selected primary-view hash, and findings. Update only the approval object in design/scene-targets/scene-target.json: status approved, reviewer scene-target-gate, selectedTargetSha256 equal to the gate-approved primary-view hash, findings copied from the review, and approvedAt as the current ISO timestamp. Validate the file as gamefactory.scene-target/v1. Do not alter candidates, prompts, geometry, component maps, hashes, or any asset; fail if the gate output and manifest disagree.

Choose the smallest production method that can faithfully realize the approved scene target. Preserve creative latitude: return exactly one outcome from direct, segment, motion_study, pixel_motion, or segment_pixel_motion. Use direct for code-native work or assets that need neither segmentation nor generated motion. Use segment only when approved whole-scene imagery should be decomposed with SAM 3. Use motion_study only when an external generated video is useful as non-runtime motion reference. Use pixel_motion when a generated motion study should be tracked and compiled into palette-locked runtime frames; add segmentation only when static scene components also need extraction. Before selecting a provider lane, verify its configured request path and prerequisites are available; never select a paid or credentialed provider merely because it exists. Write design/asset-lanes/decision.json with rationale, selected outcome, required components, source scene ids and hashes, and expected outputs. For every selected lane, also write its valid candidate-local request: sam3.request.json, video.request.json, sam3.video.request.json, and/or pixel-motion.request.json. Pin the approved scene images as references and choose contained output directories. Do not generate or integrate assets in this node.

Turn exactly one proven encounter into a coherent production slice derived from the explicitly approved gamefactory.scene-target/v1 target and state variants. Do not substitute a different visual direction. Consume the asset-lane decision and every completed extension artifact as provenance-bearing source material; a skipped lane means the planner deliberately chose another method, and a SAM 3 no_instances outcome means no usable extraction exists and must fall back to faithful regeneration or code-native construction rather than being called a successful segmentation. Author the design system, real runtime assets, typography, interaction states, motion, effects, engine capture, and gamefactory.polish-readiness/v1 manifest. Before generating UI art, preserve the approved target's exact nativeGeometry contract: viewport, baseUnitPx, borderWidthsPx, typographyPx, component footprints, and scalingRules. For every component, retain sourceViewId, crop, stateIds, and derivedFromSceneTargetSha256, then add component.production with method, sourcePath/sourceSha256, runtimePath/runtimeSha256, nativeSize, renderSize, scaling, and hash-pinned composite, comparison, or engine-capture matchEvidence. Prefer direct extraction when resolution permits; otherwise regenerate with the scene and crop as high-fidelity anchors, then composite the result back into the target layout to check the match. Build reusable panels, controls, selection, status, and result states from that contract. For raster or pixel-art direction, compile each runtime image to its final native dimensions and place it 1:1, or use a declared nine-slice region without scaling corners. Never independently downscale generated components into unrelated visual densities. Code-native structural UI is acceptable when it matches the approved target rather than default programmer chrome. Build an authored motion grammar tied to gameplay causality: anticipation, action, travel, impact, reaction, defeat, and resolution should be distinguishable where relevant. Generated or segmented assets must be deliberately cleaned, anchored, animated as required, and promoted to production before runtime use. Produce real engine-recorded evidence at evidence/captures/planning.png, evidence/captures/action.png, and evidence/captures/result.png, plus seven visibly changing frames at evidence/motion/frame-000.png through frame-006.png. Captures must come from the running Godot project at the shipping camera and show the actual named states, not reconstructed promotional composites. Remove procedural and placeholder fallbacks from every required surface. If incomplete, report visual-prototype rather than overstating maturity.

Inspect the current engine stills and motion recording, design-system hashes, polish manifest, runtime asset imports, interface-kit inventory and states, pixel-grid compliance, and deterministic scenario. Verify that motion evidence comes from the running engine and covers action causality rather than a reconstructed promo. Return pass only when evidence is current and internally consistent; otherwise return revise with exact stale, missing, or overstated claims.

Compare every production component and the current Godot capture against the approved whole-scene target and its state variants. Verify target-hash lineage, source view and crop, silhouette, material, palette, border density, typography relationship, ornament scale, native and render dimensions, and state consistency. Composite isolated components back into their approved target regions where useful. Reject unconditioned individual generations, assets derived from another target, style drift, approximate matches that change hierarchy, or a locally attractive component that weakens the complete screen. Return pass only when the assembled runtime recovers the approved scene language while remaining clear and engine-native; otherwise return revise with exact component and integration mismatches.

Judge the actual shipping-camera Godot stills and motion recording as a unified game experience. Inspect interface chrome as a first-class art surface: panels, buttons, sockets, meters, icons, focus/selected states, and results must share one native-grid contract. Compare border weight, padding, motif scale, type scale, control hierarchy, and rendered texture density across every visible component; reject arbitrary stretching, independently downscaled generated panels, oversized ornaments, collisions, or decorative geometry that contradicts interaction hierarchy. Inspect motion as a first-class system: readable anticipation, distinct role actions, travel, impact, reaction, defeat, and resolution must reinforce mechanics instead of being generic idle bob or ambient particles. Reject mixtures of generated illustration, procedural programmer UI, default typography, inconsistent pixel density, weak hierarchy, incomplete states, motionless paper-doll presentation, or asset-library incoherence. Return pass only when the representative encounter looks intentionally authored and production-ready; otherwise return revise with prioritized repairs. Always return findings.scorecard with numeric 0-100 values for focal_hierarchy, gameplay_legibility, interface_coherence, authored_specificity, target_fidelity, and motion_feedback. Always return findings.evidence with concrete observations citing each required view id planning, action, and result and the required sequence id gameplay-motion. Never inflate a score or call the game fun without human playtest evidence.

Make the final production-slice decision from the approved whole-scene target, scene review, current engine capture, component-fidelity findings, gameplay evidence, art-director findings, asset maturity, and polish manifest. Return pass only if every required surface is production, every required gate is evidenced, every runtime component is traceable to the selected scene target, and no blocker or runtime placeholder remains. Return revise rather than accepting a halfway state.
